Incorporating the April 2017 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS) into the assessment:

- Credit supply looks mixed-to-slightly tighter, not broadly easing. Banks reported tightening in auto lending standards and concerns around capital/liquidity and regulatory changes; foreign banks raised loan spreads and lowered LTVs—signals of marginally tighter conditions. CRE lending, particularly construction and land development, also showed tighter tendencies.
- Offsetting positives: some easing in credit card lending and reported willingness to extend consumer installment credit, which supports household spending at the margin.
- Net read-through: While the FOMC’s statement conveys a moderately positive, data-dependent outlook with continued accommodation and a “transitory” growth dip, SLOOS suggests bank-intermediated credit is not adding much incremental support and, in some segments, is tightening. This tempers the growth and investment impulse implied by easier financial conditions via the Fed’s reinvestment policy.

Adjusted view: still modestly positive, but less upbeat once SLOOS credit conditions are accounted for.
